text: Joints in carpentry are the connections between different pieces of wood. The most common joints are the square, round, and beveled (also known as interlocking), each designed to ensure stability and durability. The square joint involves two right-angled pieces aligned at a 90-degree angle, while the round joint uses a circular cut, creating a smooth, continuous surface. The beveled joint offers a robust connection, often found in bookshelf construction. Beyond these, there are mortise and tenon, notched and pegged, and others, each with specific uses and advantages in terms of strength and aesthetics. While varnish is often applied to furniture, it does not affect joint integrity, as the structural integrity comes from the craftsmanship of the joint itself.
